hooks.text: It was only built to last five years.
Most people think Voyager 1 is dead, but it is still talking.
Fifteen billion miles from Earth, Voyager 1 is running out of power.

title: Voyager 1's Deep Space Survival
description: How Voyager 1 outlived its five-year design to become humanity's most distant emissary in interstellar space.

beats.text: It was only built to last five years.
beats.visual: artist concept of Voyager 1 in interstellar space, NASA illustration

beats.text: Launched on September 5, 1977, the legendary metal probe quickly became the most distant human-made object from Earth.
beats.visual: Titan IIIE Centaur rocket launch carrying Voyager 1, 1977

beats.text: Voyager 1 discovered active volcanoes on Jupiter's moon Io and revealed astonishingly complex structures across Saturn's rings.
beats.visual: volcanic eruption on Io captured by Voyager 1, 1979

beats.text: The durable spacecraft officially entered interstellar space in August 2012, while blazing along at 38,000 miles per hour.
beats.visual: artist concept of the heliopause and interstellar boundary, NASA, 2012

beats.text: Now pushing past 15 billion miles away, harried human engineers are shutting down its remaining scientific instruments one by one.
beats.visual: NASA Deep Space Network 70-meter antenna dish at Goldstone, 2020

beats.text: As of 2026, only two fragile science instruments remain fully operational as it sails through the frozen cosmic void.
beats.visual: Voyager 1 spacecraft diagram showing instrument components, NASA

beats.text: And to think, when this probe launched back in 1977,
beats.visual: Voyager Golden Record cover diagram and gold-plated copper disk, 1977

better_than_last: Updated beat 7 per reviewer request to create an organic lead-in to beat 1 without repeating the hook verbatim.
